payload.name: Keep Specific Events Not Covered by General Memories
payload.description: When deciding whether to ADD or SKIP an event candidate and the only existing memory is a broader general statement, ADD the event instead of skipping it as already represented.
content: During CRUD decisions, compare an event candidate against existing memories for the same concrete occurrence: same subject, action, object, time, and emotional reaction.

If the existing memory states only a general trait, preference, or impact and does not already contain the specific event details, do not SKIP as already represented; ADD or MERGE the event candidate.
Preserve the distinct event even when it illustrates a broader theme, because later questions may ask about the specific episode or feeling.
Stop after one event per occurrence; do not add multiple paraphrases of the same event.

solves: Prevents loss of specific episodic facts during memory construction when a candidate is incorrectly skipped because a general memory about the same person or topic already exists. It preserves concrete events and feelings that may be asked about later.
